item.title: Game Theoretical Models and Applications SING21
item.content:encoded:
Annamaria Barbagallo, University of Naples Federico II

Encarnación Algaba, University of Seville

Giovanna Bimonte, University of Salerno

Francesco Ciardiello, University of Salerno

This special issue focuses on game theory as a framework for analyzing strategic interaction, cooperation, conflict, and decision-making in complex systems. It showcases recent developments in game theory alongside its diverse applications, with emphasis on interaction dynamics and collective decision-making through theoretical, practical, and interdisciplinary approaches.

The issue particularly welcomes expanded versions of papers presented at the European Meeting on Game Theory 2026 (SING21), though other relevant submissions are also encouraged. Papers based on conference presentations must be substantially revised and extended with appropriate references to the original conference versions.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Cooperative games and their applications
  • Non-cooperative games and strategic interaction
  • Mechanism design
  • Network
  • Dynamic games
  • Evolutionary games
  • Stochastic games
  • Voting, power indices, and collective decision-making
  • Auctions and market design
  • Bargaining
  • Learning and experimentation in games
  • Computational game theory
  • Applications of game theory to management, energy, health policy, industrial organization, environmental and resource economics, transportation, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and other fields

Timeline

  • April 20, 2027: Submission deadline
